title: The Negative Test on Omeprazole — Hässle Enteric-Coated Benzimidazole Patents, Acid-Activated Sulfenamide Disulfide Trapping at Gastric H+/K+-ATPase Cys813 (Comparator PDB 5YLU), CYP2C19 PK & False-Negative 13C-Urea Breath Tests

teenKit.tldr: In 15 seconds: Omeprazole turns on only inside battery-acid stomach canaliculi to covalently lock proton pumps—which also starves H. pylori urease and causes false-negative breath and stool tests unless stopped two weeks early.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Testing for H. pylori while a patient is still taking a proton pump inhibitor misses active ulcer-causing infections and sends clinicians down the wrong diagnostic path.
keyTakeaways: Omeprazole is an enteric-coated weak base that concentrates in acidic parietal-cell canaliculi and rearranges into a reactive sulfenamide that forms a disulfide bond with Cys813 on gastric H+/K+-ATPase.
Polymorphic CYP2C19 metabolism creates major exposure differences between ultrarapid and poor metabolizers.
By raising gastric pH and suppressing bacterial load and urease activity, omeprazole causes false-negative 13C-urea breath tests and stool antigen assays, requiring a 2-week washout before testing.

vocab.meaning: A drug rearranged by target-site chemistry (here, extreme acid) into an active species that forms a covalent bond.
A non-invasive H. pylori test measuring isotopically labeled CO2 exhaled when bacterial urease splits swallowed 13C-urea.
The hepatic cytochrome P450 enzyme responsible for clearing first-generation proton pump inhibitors.

quiz.question: Why does omeprazole selectively inhibit proton pumps in stomach parietal cells rather than neutral tissues?
options: Its weak-base pyridine/benzimidazole core traps and acid-rearranges into an active sulfenamide specifically at canalicular pH ~1
quiz.explanation: Protonation trapping and acid-catalyzed conversion to the reactive sulfenamide require the extreme acidity of actively secreting parietal canaliculi.
